https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize.body:
## Problem

Independent harness runs should be able to plan and edit concurrently, while builds and verification wait their turn and continue automatically when execution becomes available. Some idle time is acceptable; simplicity, reliable continuation and preserved independent verification matter more than maximum throughput.

This is a deliberately narrower replacement proposal for https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/issues/40. The user reports that its implementation attempt has run for eight hours and intends to shut it down. Do not inherit #40's general resource scheduler or cross-machine requirements. Filing this issue neither closes #40 nor terminates its running work.

## Required outcome

Support Linux, one host and one common Git repository with isolated worktrees. Reuse the existing Git-backed harness records and artifact publication. Provide a small, movable execution entry point backed by one supervised runner and one serial lane for heavy commands. Planning, reasoning and source editing may overlap; all roles' builds, tests, benchmarks and exploratory heavy executions use the serial lane.

Example interface (spelling is illustrative):

```sh
harness-exec --run RUN_ID --cwd BUILD_DIR -- ctest --output-on-failure
```

The entry point submits, waits for and returns the actual job result. A waiting agent/chat need not remain alive for an accepted job and its workflow to continue. Persisted JSON alone is not autonomous execution.

## Acceptance criteria

1. **Independent run records.** Replace implicit singleton selection with explicit run identity. Preserve isolated source/build/output paths, one owner for the same issue/deliverable, existing role independence, candidate/plan/attempt binding, bounded repair and publication gates. Completing one run cannot clear another. Preserve existing history and live work during migration; reconcile any partial #40 implementation before changing it.

2. **Reuse state and publication.** Retain one artifact branch and a short repository transaction lock. Reload its latest tree, validate the selected run's revision, and update only that run. Another run's ordinary checkpoint is refreshable contention, not a failed run. Serialize checkpoint/publication and preserve exact publication confirmation and uncertain-write recovery. Do not merge arbitrary state JSON or replay external effects blindly.

3. **Encapsulated serial execution.** Keep the entry point, runner, tests and detailed documentation within the harness hierarchy or its established successor. Callers do not implement their own flock logic. Use one stable host-wide lock and a simple ordered queue derived from durable job records; no resource graph or capacity scheduler. Record run/role/attempt, source identity, command/cwd and execution limits before launch. Waiting consumes neither command timeout nor repair allowance; explicitly reconcile the existing overall deadline policy rather than silently extending an active run.

4. **Real autonomous continuation.** Ordinary contention causes waiting, followed by automatic execution and continuation through the next authorized workflow action, without prompts or another chat message. Use an actual supported agent-launch adapter, such as a validated noninteractive CLI backend, and preserve fresh role contexts and independent checks. Confirm required tools/report interfaces work through that backend. A service wrapping the state helper alone is insufficient. Supervise the runner with restart enabled; reconstruct pending work and reconcile in-flight work before new admission. Document restart, logout and reboot behavior precisely.

5. **Safe process ownership.** One runner controls admission. A killed wrapper must not release the next job while old descendants can still act. Use managed process containment and cleanup, with a durable in-flight marker; establish quiescence before admitting another job after failure/restart. Preserve interrupted/failure evidence. Retry only reconciled, repeatable operations; reconcile PR/comment mutations through authoritative lookup. Unknown cleanup blocks the lane with an accurate reason, never a fabricated pass.

6. **Movable, versioned interface.** Script/package paths may move without changing the shared lock/queue identity or losing waiting work. Runtime storage lives outside source/build checkouts. Never unlink a live lock. Pin the executor/protocol for accepted jobs; activate incompatible updates only through a documented drain/handoff between jobs. A harness self-update cannot start a second executor over the same resource or silently change another run's rules.

## Required verification

Use disposable repositories, bounded processes and assertion-bearing tests:

- Two runs overlap planning/editing, retain independent state, and complete without report/approval crossover; same-issue starts admit one owner.
- Builds/tests from every role never overlap. A queued job executes and its workflow advances automatically when the lane is freed.
- Another run advances artifact history while a job waits; the waiting run continues without manual reconciliation.
- Restart while waiting and while running; include a killed wrapper with a surviving grandchild. No successor starts before cleanup/reconciliation.
- Interrupt after execution but before result recording, and around artifact/PR publication. Preserve evidence without inventing success or duplicating external effects.
- Move the harness entry point with waiting/running jobs; stable lock/queue identity prevents overlap and stranded jobs.
- Exercise the actual agent backend end to end, including independent verification and the permitted publication outcome. Mock process fixtures alone do not establish autonomous agent continuation.

Run the relevant existing harness regressions. Report unsupported, failed and incomplete checks honestly. Research probes confirmed blocking-flock handoff and reproduced premature release after wrapper death; they do not prove the proposed runner exists.

## Scope and relationships

Parent: https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/issues/9. Narrow replacement proposal for https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/issues/40; do not copy all its acceptance criteria or make it a prerequisite. Related https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/issues/43 owns change-scoped verification/evidence execution: integrate at the execution boundary and avoid duplicating its manifest/test-selection logic.

Out of scope: multiple hosts or independent clone writers, distributed leases, databases, hierarchical/capacity scheduling, sandbox infrastructure, automatic merge, and unattended live Steam restoration. Existing unsupported mandatory gates remain incomplete; exclusions do not authorize skipping them. No live Steam/GPU experiments, service installation or new implementation run are authorized merely by this filing.

Completing, closing or wrapping up A removes only A from active discovery; B remains selectable with its approvals and queued work intact. A selector is mandatory when ambiguity exists; normal new workflow uses explicit selector even with one active run.

A and B start from one artifact tip. B commits first. A ordinary checkpoint reloads latest records, confirms A expected revision still matches, and commits only A changes on B latest tree without manual reconciliation.

Same selected-run revision change fails closed. Tampered historical bytes, dropped immutable evidence, policy/endpoint changes and divergent remote history still fail. All source history remains separate from orphan artifacts.

Inject publication failure/lost response before and after push; exact-tip confirmation is required and authoritative readback precedes retry. No external effect is redispatched because another run advanced the artifact tip.

One supported submit-and-wait CLI accepts argv without shell reinterpretation and returns actual exit/signal/timeout result with separate stdout/stderr references. Invalid/missing tool/cwd/identity/limit fails honestly.

Durable job records precede launch and contain run/root/role/attempt, source SHA/cleanliness identity, cwd/argv, protocol/package digest, timeout and authorized continuation. FIFO sequence comes from durable records under stable host lock.

Planner, implementer, unit-checker and final-checker heavy command fixtures from two worktrees produce nonoverlapping start/end intervals; source editing/planning can progress outside the lane. No caller supplies its own flock.

Waiting does not start command timeout or consume repair attempts. The existing absolute run deadline remains unchanged: expiry while queued produces explicit incomplete/awaiting-decision and no launch; extension requires existing explicit budget-extension authority.

With lane held, accept B job then kill the submitting/waiting wrapper/chat process. After A exits, B executes and its saved bound continuation launches/advances the next authorized workflow action automatically.

B waits while A advances artifact history; B continuation consumes only current selected-run revision and succeeds automatically. Same-run material input change invalidates stale queued action instead of refreshing it silently.

Saved continuation is consumed exactly once through current reducer/idempotency records; malformed or stale reports, missing backend, exhausted budget, human approval boundary and unsupported attachment interfaces produce accurate blocked/incomplete status, never success.

Real systemd cgroup fixture spawns a grandchild that starts a new session and keeps writing. Kill the wrapper, restart runner, and verify successor never starts before all owned descendant writes cease and the exact owned cgroup is empty.

Restart while waiting reconstructs FIFO. Restart during launch/execution reads durable in-flight unit identity; it reattaches to provably owned work or stops it and verifies quiescence before admitting another command.

A missing/unqueryable unit, unavailable user bus, changed unit invocation or failed cleanup blocks lane with retained interrupted/uncertain evidence. PID disappearance alone cannot release lane. Stopping the runner cannot expose still-running children to a second runner.

Timeout kills the full owned group under finite stop/kill limits; real nonzero exits, signals and interruption remain distinguishable. No automatic retry of a nonrepeatable command without positive no-send/reconciliation evidence.

Crash after child exit before result recording retains output/status custody and resolves from owned unit/job completion facts or records interrupted/unknown; it never invents pass or blindly reruns the command.

Crash around report ingest/continuation enqueue and PR/comment dispatch/returned/readback/publication boundaries preserves stable operation IDs and observes authoritative fixture service before retry. Lost create/comment response yields one effect, uncertain absence stays incomplete.
Known failing source stops further authorized success-path gates; completed failure evidence is retained and successors requiring acceptance cannot run.

Move/copy the entrypoint package while jobs wait and run; both entrypoints resolve the same out-of-checkout host runtime/lock/queue. Accepted work continues through pinned immutable executor package and cannot overlap a second runner.
Runtime/job symlink or ownership violations fail closed. Source/build checkout is never default runtime storage. No operation unlinks/replaces a live lock inode.

Changed protocol/package cannot silently reinterpret accepted jobs or another run rules. Documented drain/handoff refuses active work, validates cleanup, retains pending records and activates compatible pinned work only at a safe boundary.

original.requirement:
## Problem

Independent harness runs should be able to plan and edit concurrently, while builds and verification wait their turn and continue automatically when execution becomes available. Some idle time is acceptable; simplicity, reliable continuation and preserved independent verification matter more than maximum throughput.

This is a deliberately narrower replacement proposal for https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/issues/40. The user reports that its implementation attempt has run for eight hours and intends to shut it down. Do not inherit #40's general resource scheduler or cross-machine requirements. Filing this issue neither closes #40 nor terminates its running work.

## Required outcome

Support Linux, one host and one common Git repository with isolated worktrees. Reuse the existing Git-backed harness records and artifact publication. Provide a small, movable execution entry point backed by one supervised runner and one serial lane for heavy commands. Planning, reasoning and source editing may overlap; all roles' builds, tests, benchmarks and exploratory heavy executions use the serial lane.

Example interface (spelling is illustrative):

```sh
harness-exec --run RUN_ID --cwd BUILD_DIR -- ctest --output-on-failure
```

The entry point submits, waits for and returns the actual job result. A waiting agent/chat need not remain alive for an accepted job and its workflow to continue. Persisted JSON alone is not autonomous execution.

## Acceptance criteria

1. **Independent run records.** Replace implicit singleton selection with explicit run identity. Preserve isolated source/build/output paths, one owner for the same issue/deliverable, existing role independence, candidate/plan/attempt binding, bounded repair and publication gates. Completing one run cannot clear another. Preserve existing history and live work during migration; reconcile any partial #40 implementation before changing it.

2. **Reuse state and publication.** Retain one artifact branch and a short repository transaction lock. Reload its latest tree, validate the selected run's revision, and update only that run. Another run's ordinary checkpoint is refreshable contention, not a failed run. Serialize checkpoint/publication and preserve exact publication confirmation and uncertain-write recovery. Do not merge arbitrary state JSON or replay external effects blindly.

3. **Encapsulated serial execution.** Keep the entry point, runner, tests and detailed documentation within the harness hierarchy or its established successor. Callers do not implement their own flock logic. Use one stable host-wide lock and a simple ordered queue derived from durable job records; no resource graph or capacity scheduler. Record run/role/attempt, source identity, command/cwd and execution limits before launch. Waiting consumes neither command timeout nor repair allowance; explicitly reconcile the existing overall deadline policy rather than silently extending an active run.

4. **Real autonomous continuation.** Ordinary contention causes waiting, followed by automatic execution and continuation through the next authorized workflow action, without prompts or another chat message. Use an actual supported agent-launch adapter, such as a validated noninteractive CLI backend, and preserve fresh role contexts and independent checks. Confirm required tools/report interfaces work through that backend. A service wrapping the state helper alone is insufficient. Supervise the runner with restart enabled; reconstruct pending work and reconcile in-flight work before new admission. Document restart, logout and reboot behavior precisely.

5. **Safe process ownership.** One runner controls admission. A killed wrapper must not release the next job while old descendants can still act. Use managed process containment and cleanup, with a durable in-flight marker; establish quiescence before admitting another job after failure/restart. Preserve interrupted/failure evidence. Retry only reconciled, repeatable operations; reconcile PR/comment mutations through authoritative lookup. Unknown cleanup blocks the lane with an accurate reason, never a fabricated pass.

6. **Movable, versioned interface.** Script/package paths may move without changing the shared lock/queue identity or losing waiting work. Runtime storage lives outside source/build checkouts. Never unlink a live lock. Pin the executor/protocol for accepted jobs; activate incompatible updates only through a documented drain/handoff between jobs. A harness self-update cannot start a second executor over the same resource or silently change another run's rules.

## Required verification

Use disposable repositories, bounded processes and assertion-bearing tests:

- Two runs overlap planning/editing, retain independent state, and complete without report/approval crossover; same-issue starts admit one owner.
- Builds/tests from every role never overlap. A queued job executes and its workflow advances automatically when the lane is freed.
- Another run advances artifact history while a job waits; the waiting run continues without manual reconciliation.
- Restart while waiting and while running; include a killed wrapper with a surviving grandchild. No successor starts before cleanup/reconciliation.
- Interrupt after execution but before result recording, and around artifact/PR publication. Preserve evidence without inventing success or duplicating external effects.
- Move the harness entry point with waiting/running jobs; stable lock/queue identity prevents overlap and stranded jobs.
- Exercise the actual agent backend end to end, including independent verification and the permitted publication outcome. Mock process fixtures alone do not establish autonomous agent continuation.

Run the relevant existing harness regressions. Report unsupported, failed and incomplete checks honestly. Research probes confirmed blocking-flock handoff and reproduced premature release after wrapper death; they do not prove the proposed runner exists.

## Scope and relationships

Parent: https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/issues/9. Narrow replacement proposal for https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/issues/40; do not copy all its acceptance criteria or make it a prerequisite. Related https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/issues/43 owns change-scoped verification/evidence execution: integrate at the execution boundary and avoid duplicating its manifest/test-selection logic.

Out of scope: multiple hosts or independent clone writers, distributed leases, databases, hierarchical/capacity scheduling, sandbox infrastructure, automatic merge, and unattended live Steam restoration. Existing unsupported mandatory gates remain incomplete; exclusions do not authorize skipping them. No live Steam/GPU experiments, service installation or new implementation run are authorized merely by this filing.

Every heavy process must use serial lane; tests of the executor necessarily create isolated disposable authority namespaces inside one outer serialized gate. Do not claim global enforcement against arbitrary unrelated processes.

Fresh full regressions plus actual backend checks for implementer/unit checker/final checker must fit remaining original four-hour budget. A long test cannot silently extend command/run limits or weaken union requirements.

Filesystem atomicity, cgroup invocation identity, service restart races, result-before-record crash and external effects need failure controls. Unknown means blocked/incomplete, never requeue automatically.
Migration touches current workflow authority: only coordinator writes canonical state; preserve exact accepted attempts/budgets and old helper usable until migration contract is verified.

boundaries: Planning/reasoning/editing may overlap. Every role build/test/benchmark/exploratory heavy execution uses supported lane interface. Cooperative harness process custody is not a hostile-command sandbox or proof against unrelated desktop processes.

Preserve all existing acceptance/role/checker/publication policies. Existing failed/unsupported mandatory checks remain blockers. No native Fossilize/Steam/GPU work is necessary for this harness-only change.
Use existing runner selection/evidence API; integrate at command execution boundary without implementing issue43 manifest/provider selection.
